translation_en: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Affan narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us: Yahya ibn Sa‘id informed me, from Ubayd ibn Hunayn, from Ibn Abbas, who said: I went with Umar, and when we reached Marr al-Zahran—then he related the full story, similar to Sulayman ibn Bilal’s report—except that he said: I asked, “What about the two women?” He said, “Hafsah and Umm Salamah.” It also adds: I went to the apartments, and there was crying in every house. It further adds: He swore to abstain from them for a month, and when twenty-nine days had passed, he went down to them.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us; these are Abu Bakr’s words. They said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, who heard Ubayd ibn Hunayn—the freedman of al-Abbas—say: I heard Ibn Abbas say: I wanted to ask Umar about the two women who had joined together against the Messenger of Allah during his time, but I waited a year without finding a suitable opportunity. Then I accompanied him to Mecca. When we reached Marr al-Zahran, he went to attend to a need and said, “Bring me a water container.” I brought it to him. When he had finished and returned, I began pouring water over him and mentioned the matter. I said, “Commander of the Faithful, who were the two women?” I had not even finished speaking when he said, “Aishah and Hafsah.”
